title: Jeremiah Chapter 46 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 46 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 46 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 46.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 46, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD which came to Jeremiah
Against Egypt, against the army of Pharaohnecho
Order ye the buckler and shield
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD which came to Jeremiah
questions.explanation: This is found in Jeremiah 46:1, stating that the chapter begins with the word of the LORD to Jeremiah.

questions.question: Who is the king of Egypt mentioned in Jeremiah 46?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:2 identifies Pharaohnecho as the king of Egypt against whom the word of the LORD came.

questions.question: What action is commanded in Jeremiah 46:3?
options: Order ye the buckler and shield
questions.correctAnswer: Order ye the buckler and shield
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:3 specifically commands to order the buckler and shield as a preparation for battle.

questions.question: What are the horsemen instructed to do in Jeremiah 46:4?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:4 includes all these commands to the horsemen in preparation for battle.

questions.question: What has caused the mighty ones to be dismayed according to Jeremiah 46:5?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:5 states that fear was round about, causing the mighty ones to turn back.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 46:6, where will the mighty man stumble and fall?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:6 specifies that they shall stumble and fall toward the north by the river Euphrates.

questions.question: What imagery is used to describe Egypt in Jeremiah 46:8?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:8 describes Egypt rising up like a flood, emphasizing its overwhelming nature.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 46:9, who are called to come up and rage?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:9 specifically calls the Ethiopians and the Libyans to come up and rage.

questions.question: What day is described in Jeremiah 46:10?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:10 states that it is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance.

questions.question: What will the sword do on the day of vengeance according to Jeremiah 46:10?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:10 describes the sword as devouring and being made drunk with blood on the day of vengeance.

questions.question: The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah against which group?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:1 states that the word of the LORD came against the Gentiles.

questions.question: True or False: The army of Pharaohnecho was defeated by Nebuchadrezzar.
questions.explanation: This is stated in Jeremiah 46:2, where it mentions Nebuchadrezzar smiting the army of Pharaohnecho.

questions.question: True or False: The horsemen are told to stand down in Jeremiah 46.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:4 instructs horsemen to get up and stand forth, indicating they are not to stand down.

questions.question: True or False: Fear was not a factor for the mighty ones according to the text.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:5 indicates that fear was indeed a factor, causing the mighty ones to turn back.

questions.question: True or False: Egypt intended to cover the earth and destroy the city according to Jeremiah 46:8.
questions.explanation: While Egypt rises up like a flood, Jeremiah 46:8 specifically states its intention to destroy the city and its inhabitants, not to cover the earth in general.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 46 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 46 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 46:11 say about the use of many medicines in Egypt?
options: In vain shalt thou use many medicines; for thou shalt not be cured
Many medicines shall heal thee completely
Medicines will bring temporary relief only
Medicines shall be scarce in Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: In vain shalt thou use many medicines; for thou shalt not be cured
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:11 explicitly states that using many medicines will be in vain and there will be no cure.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 46:12 promise will happen if the mighty man does not stumble?
options: They will flee and not return
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:12 says the mighty man hath stumbled against the mighty, and they are fallen both together, linking the stumbling to their fall.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 46:14, what are the people of Egypt commanded to do in preparation for the coming threat?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:14 instructs the people to stand fast and prepare themselves for the sword that shall devour round about them.

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 46:15 and 46:16 together explain the defeat of Egypt's valiant men?
options: The LORD drove them, causing many to fall, one upon another
They fled because they were outnumbered
They were betrayed by their allies
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD drove them, causing many to fall, one upon another
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:15 explains that the LORD drove the valiant men away, and 46:16 describes many falling one upon another as they tried to escape the oppressing sword.

questions.question: What practical lesson can Christians learn from the warning in Jeremiah 46:11 about relying on many medicines in vain?
options: True healing comes from God, not just human remedies
One should avoid seeking any help in trouble
questions.correctAnswer: True healing comes from God, not just human remedies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:11 shows that despite many medicines, Egypt will not be cured, implying the need for divine intervention for true healing.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 46:19 encourage believers to prepare spiritually for hardship?
options: Furnish thyself to go into captivity
questions.correctAnswer: Furnish thyself to go into captivity
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:19 advises preparing oneself for captivity, which can metaphorically teach believers to be ready for trials in faith.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 46:20 symbolize Egypt as, and what is coming upon it?
options: A very fair heifer; destruction cometh
questions.correctAnswer: A very fair heifer; destruction cometh
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:20 compares Egypt to a fair heifer but warns that destruction is coming out of the north.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 46:17 describe Pharaoh king of Egypt in contrast to his previous strength?
options: Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise
Pharaoh has made a strong alliance
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:17 states Pharaoh is but a noise, indicating his power and influence has diminished.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase in Jeremiah 46:18 comparing the LORD's coming to Tabor and Carmel?
options: It emphasizes the certainty and majesty of the LORD's arrival
It suggests the LORD will come secretly
It says the LORD will come only at night
It means the LORD will delay His coming
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the certainty and majesty of the LORD's arrival
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:18 uses prominent mountains to symbolize the sure and majestic coming of the LORD.

questions.question: What practical advice about facing adversity can be drawn from Jeremiah 46:14's call to "stand fast, and prepare thee"?
options: Be steadfast and ready in faith when challenges arise
Avoid any confrontation at all costs
Wait passively for problems to resolve
questions.correctAnswer: Be steadfast and ready in faith when challenges arise
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:14's command encourages active, steadfast preparation, a principle applicable in spiritual challenges.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 46:16, what did the fallen men say after their defeat?
options: Arise, and let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity
We will fight until the last man
questions.correctAnswer: Arise, and let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:16 records the defeated men urging each other to return to their homeland from the oppressing sword.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 46:15 reveal about the reason Egypt's valiant men were swept away?
options: Because the LORD did drive them
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD did drive them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:15 clearly attributes the defeat and flight of Egypt's mighty men to the LORD's driving them away.

questions.question: What is the meaning behind the cry filling the land mentioned in Jeremiah 46:12?
options: The nations have heard of Egypt's shame and cry of distress
The harvest festival is taking place
A new king has been crowned
questions.correctAnswer: The nations have heard of Egypt's shame and cry of distress
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:12 indicates that the nations heard Egypt's shame and cry, signaling widespread distress.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 46:18 declares the LORD of hosts lives and will come as surely as Tabor is among the mountains.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:18 confirms the LORD of hosts' living nature and certain coming, comparing it to Tabor among mountains.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 46:11 encourages the daughter of Egypt to rely on many medicines for a complete cure.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:11 states that many medicines will be used in vain and Egypt will not be cured, so reliance on medicines is not encouraged.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 46 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 46.

questions.question: What happens to the hired men in Egypt according to Jeremiah 46:21?
options: They are turned back and flee
questions.correctAnswer: They are turned back and flee
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:21 states that her hired men are in the midst of her like fatted bullocks; for they also are turned back, and are fled away together.

questions.question: How does the voice of the army come against Egypt in Jeremiah 46:22?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 46:22, it is said that the voice thereof shall go like a serpent, indicating a stealthy and dangerous approach.

questions.question: What does the LORD say will happen to Egypt's forest in Jeremiah 46:23?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:23 states that they shall cut down her forest, signifying the total destruction that is prophesied for Egypt.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 46:24, who will confound the daughter of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:24 indicates that the daughter of Egypt shall be confounded; she shall be delivered into the hand of the people of the north, referring to Babylonian forces.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to Jacob in Jeremiah 46:27?
options: He will save him from afar
He will lead him to battle
questions.correctAnswer: He will save him from afar
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:27 reassures Jacob that the LORD will save him from afar off, showing God's continued protection and care for His people.

questions.question: What does God promise about the nations in Jeremiah 46:28?
options: He will make a full end of them
He will correct them in measure
He will leave them wholly unpunished
questions.correctAnswer: He will correct them in measure
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:28 states that God will make a full end of all the nations whither He has driven Jacob, but will correct him in measure, indicating a balance of justice.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'fatted' in Jeremiah 46:21 imply about the bullocks?
questions.explanation: The word 'fatted' refers to animals that are well-fed and fattened for slaughter, symbolizing the state of the hired men in Egypt who are unprepared to fight.

questions.question: Which literary technique is demonstrated in Jeremiah 46:10 with the phrase 'the day of vengeance'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'the day of vengeance' in Jeremiah 46:10 foreshadows the impending judgment and destruction that will come upon Egypt, indicating a future event.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of punishment for nations as seen in Jeremiah 46:25?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:10 also speaks of the judgment and punishment of Egypt, connecting to the theme of divine retribution found in Jeremiah 46:25.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of restoration seen in Jeremiah 46:27?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:1 speaks of comfort and restoration for God's people, echoing the promise of salvation found in Jeremiah 46:27.

questions.question: What comes before the statement in Jeremiah 46:21 regarding the hired men?
options: The voice shall go like a serpent
The daughter of Egypt shall be confounded
The LORD will punish the multitude of No
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will punish the multitude of No
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:25 precedes the statement about hired men in verse 21, setting the context of impending judgment on Egypt.

questions.question: What follows the promise in Jeremiah 46:27 about Jacob's safety?
questions.explanation: Following Jeremiah 46:27, the promise continues in verse 28, stating that Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease, emphasizing God's protection.

questions.question: The army coming against Egypt is described as having what characteristic in Jeremiah 46:22?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:22 describes the army's approach with axes, indicating a brutal force, but also implies that they are numerous as they cut down her forest.

questions.question: The LORD's promise in Jeremiah 46:28 assures Jacob that he will not be what?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 46:28, it is stated that God will not make a full end of Jacob but will correct him in measure, signifying His mercy.

questions.question: Jeremiah 46:10 indicates that the day of the LORD is a day of what?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:10 indicates that it is a day of vengeance, not peace, showing that it is a time for judgment rather than tranquility.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 46 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 46 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 46:10 teach about God's nature?
options: God executes divine vengeance against His adversaries
God passively observes human conflicts without intervention
God is indifferent to the fate of nations
questions.correctAnswer: God executes divine vengeance against His adversaries
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:10 states, 'For this is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries,' demonstrating God's active role in judgment and vengeance.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sinfulness is taught in Jeremiah 46:11?
options: Human efforts and remedies are ineffective against God's judgment
Human wisdom can always find a cure for calamity
Sin does not result in consequences for nations
God will ultimately abandon His covenant people
questions.correctAnswer: Human efforts and remedies are ineffective against God's judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:11 says, 'in vain shalt thou use many medicines; for thou shalt not be cured,' indicating that human attempts to fix the problem are futile under divine judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about salvation is expressed in Jeremiah 46:27?
options: God promises to save Jacob and restore his people from captivity
Salvation is earned by military might and alliances
God will abandon Israel entirely to their enemies
Salvation is dependent on human wisdom alone
questions.correctAnswer: God promises to save Jacob and restore his people from captivity
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:27 states, 'I will save thee from afar off, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and be in rest and at ease,' showing God's promise of restoration and salvation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 46:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:18, where the LORD declares the certainty of His judgment like 'Tabor among the mountains,' showcases God's sovereign control over history and nations.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 46:28 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:28 emphasizes God's justice in not making a full end of Israel but correcting them in measure, illustrating His righteous judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 46:26 connect to the broader biblical theme of exile and restoration?
options: It foretells captivity followed by eventual reinhabitation, aligning with Israel's exile and return
It predicts permanent destruction without hope of restoration
It portrays exile as a punishment without divine purpose
It denies any future hope for the nation of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It foretells captivity followed by eventual reinhabitation, aligning with Israel's exile and return
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:26 says, 'and afterward it shall be inhabited, as in the days of old,' connecting to the biblical motif of exile and God’s promise of restoration.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 46:7-8 prepare for the theme of divine judgment elsewhere in Scripture?
options: By depicting Egypt as a flood overwhelmed by God's sovereign purposes
By emphasizing human military power as ultimate
By portraying God's judgment as arbitrary and unjust
By suggesting that nations are invincible
questions.correctAnswer: By depicting Egypt as a flood overwhelmed by God's sovereign purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 liken Egypt to a flood that God will overcome, setting the stage for the motif of God's sovereign judgment on nations as seen in prophetic literature.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 46:15 and Jeremiah 46:21 teach about human responsibility and divine judgment?
options: Human failure is ultimately caused by God's sovereign driving and visitation
Human strength can overcome divine judgment
God's judgment is unrelated to human actions
Humans are fully autonomous in their failures
questions.correctAnswer: Human failure is ultimately caused by God's sovereign driving and visitation
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:15 says 'because the LORD did drive them,' and 46:21 mentions 'the day of their calamity was come upon them,' showing divine causation in human defeat.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 46:25 and Jeremiah 46:28 teach about God's justice and mercy toward Israel and the nations?
options: God punishes nations severely but corrects Israel with measured discipline
God punishes Israel more harshly than other nations
God shows no mercy to any nation or people
God's justice is capricious and inconsistent
questions.correctAnswer: God punishes nations severely but corrects Israel with measured discipline
questions.explanation: Verse 25 declares punishment on Egypt and its gods, while 46:28 promises correction but not destruction for Israel, reflecting both justice and mercy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 46:19 and Jeremiah 46:24 teach about the consequences of sin for Egypt?
options: Egypt will be desolate and delivered into the hands of enemies due to sin
Egypt will be exalted above all nations
Egypt will be restored without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt will be desolate and delivered into the hands of enemies due to sin
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:19 speaks of captivity and desolation of Noph, and 46:24 states Egypt will be delivered into the hand of the people of the north, showing judgment consequences.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jeremiah 46:27-28 teaches that God arbitrarily punishes Israel without hope. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God promises salvation and measured correction, not arbitrary punishment
God punishes Israel infinitely without mercy
God is indifferent to Israel's fate
questions.correctAnswer: God promises salvation and measured correction, not arbitrary punishment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:27-28 clearly states God will save Jacob and correct him in measure, showing hope and purposeful discipline rather than arbitrary punishment.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine sovereignty is taught in Jeremiah 46:6?
options: God controls the outcome of battle so that none may escape
God allows humans full control over battle outcomes
God is unaware of human conflict
God is powerless to stop warfare
questions.correctAnswer: God controls the outcome of battle so that none may escape
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says 'Let not the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape; they shall stumble, and fall,' indicating God's sovereign control in judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 46:23 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:23 describes the army as 'more than the grasshoppers, and are innumerable,' showing God's power to bring overwhelming forces against Egypt, demonstrating omnipotence.

questions.question: What theological synthesis is taught by Jeremiah 46:13 and Jeremiah 46:14 regarding God's prophetic revelation and human responsibility?
options: God reveals coming judgment so that people may prepare, yet judgment is certain
God hides His plans from humans
Prophets are unreliable in declaring future events
Human preparation can prevent divine judgment entirely
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals coming judgment so that people may prepare, yet judgment is certain
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:13-14 commands the declaration and preparation for the coming sword, highlighting divine revelation and the certainty of judgment despite human preparation.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 46:22-23 contribute to the biblical narrative arc of divine judgment on idolatrous nations?
options: It depicts God's judgment as unstoppable and thorough against Egypt's defenses
It suggests idolatrous nations are immune to judgment
It portrays God's judgment as weak and ineffective
It denies that God judges nations
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts God's judgment as unstoppable and thorough against Egypt's defenses
questions.explanation: Verses 22-23 describe an overwhelming attacking force that will 'cut down her forest,' symbolizing God's comprehensive judgment on Egypt, an idolatrous nation.
